chief_complaint: severe ear pain, high fever, and protrusion of the right outer ear with redness and tenderness over the mastoid bone behind the ear
hpi_details: 4-year-old girl with untreated acute otitis media presenting with postauricular erythema, swelling, tenderness over the mastoid process, and anterior-inferior displacement of the right auricle, requiring IV antibiotics and urgent ENT consultation. Surgical drainage or mastoidectomy may be needed if complications are present or she fails medical treatment.
ideas: She thinks the ear infection spread into the tender bone behind the ear because they did not finish the last course of drops.
concerns: She is worried her daughter might permanently lose her hearing or need a dangerous operation on her skull.
expectations: She hopes to get strong intravenous antibiotics so her daughter will not need surgery.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute mastoiditis (complication of otitis media).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Uncomplicated otitis media without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Postauricular swelling and erythema.

red_flags: Severe headache, neck stiffness, repeated vomiting, confusion, or facial weakness requires emergency escalation

must_ask.objective: Confirm the recent ear infection history
must_ask.say: Has she had an ear infection recently that wasn't fully treated?

must_ask.objective: Ask about the ear position and swelling behind the ear
must_ask.say: Have you noticed the ear sticking out more than usual, or swelling behind it?
How high has her fever been, and how long has it lasted?

must_ask.objective: Ask about pain severity and irritability
must_ask.say: How much pain does she seem to be in, and has she been unusually fussy?

must_ask.objective: Explain the urgent IV antibiotic and ENT plan

history.answer: My 4-year-old daughter has severe pain in her right ear and a high fever, and the bone behind her ear is red and swollen.
Her right ear started hurting about five days ago after a mild cold, but the red swelling behind her ear appeared yesterday morning.
It is very severe, and she screams and clutches her right ear constantly, especially at night when she cannot sleep.
Touching or pressing behind her ear makes her cry in pain, but pulling her earlobe doesn't bother her as much, and chewing does not seem to make it worse.
history.topic: Pain on pulling ear or chewing

history.answer: A small amount of cloudy yellowish discharge came out of her right ear yesterday, but there was no blood or bad odor.
She seems to have trouble hearing when we talk softly on her right side, as if that ear is completely blocked.
She has not mentioned any ringing sounds, and she is walking steadily without any spinning dizziness.
She developed a high fever up to 39 degrees Celsius two days ago, following a runny nose and mild cough last week.
Her face looks completely even when she cries or smiles, and I haven't noticed any blisters around or inside her ear.
The area behind her right ear is red, warm, and swollen, pushing her ear forward, but she does not have a stiff neck, vomiting, or extreme drowsiness.
history.topic: Swelling behind ear and red flags

history.answer: No, she has not been swimming or taking baths where water entered her ears, and I never clean inside her ear with cotton swabs.
No, she has had no falls, ear trauma, or foreign objects inserted into her ear.
No, we have not flown on an airplane or traveled to higher elevations recently.
No, she does not complain of tooth pain, and her jaw opens and closes normally without clicking.
She has no sore throat, and she can swallow fluids without difficulty.
She had an ear infection three months ago that improved with medicine, but she has not taken any antibiotics for this current illness.
She has no history of diabetes, immune system problems, or other chronic illnesses.
She has been very irritable, constantly tugging at her right ear and refusing solid food, though she still sips water.
I think her ear infection spread into the bone behind her ear because we didn't finish all the medicine last time.
I'm terrified that she might permanently lose her hearing or need a dangerous operation on her skull.
I'm hoping you can give her some strong IV antibiotics so she won't have to undergo surgery.
She has no major chronic medical problems.
She has never had surgery, ear tube placement, or hospital stays.
I gave her children's ibuprofen and acetaminophen for the fever and pain, but she is not taking any other medications or antibiotics.
She has no known allergies to any medications, foods, or latex.
She was born full-term through an uncomplicated vaginal delivery with no neonatal complications.
She has met all developmental milestones on time and is growing along normal percentiles.
Her routine childhood immunizations are completely up to date, including the pneumococcal vaccines.
She attends daycare three days a week where other toddlers have had colds, and no one smokes in our home or around her.
There is no family history of recurrent ear infections, hearing impairment, or immune deficiencies.

exam.finding: An irritable, ill-appearing 4-year-old girl clutching the right side of her head, consolable by her mother.
Temperature 38.9°C, pulse 124/min, respiratory rate 24/min, blood pressure 98/62 mmHg, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.

Erythema, swelling, and marked tenderness over the right mastoid with anterior-inferior displacement of the right auricle; otoscopy reveals an erythematous, bulging right tympanic membrane with obscured landmarks, while the left ear is normal.
Reduced behavioral response to conversational and whispered voice on the right side compared to the left; formal tuning fork testing deferred due to age.
Mild clear nasal discharge; oral mucosa is moist, posterior oropharynx is clear without tonsillar exudates, and dentition is healthy.
Small, slightly tender right anterior cervical lymph nodes; no fluctuant cervical masses.
Facial symmetry is intact with symmetric smiling, eye closure, and forehead wrinkling; no facial droop or weakness.
Supple neck with full active and passive flexion; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
